fluff.overview:
The Ninja-To was introduced in 3062 by Independence Weaponry of Quentin as a dedicated C3 slave platform for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Named for the straight-bladed sword favored by ninja in ancient Japan, the sixty-five-ton heavy BattleMech was designed to complement other C3-equipped designs in the Combine's growing roster of networked 'Mechs. Independence Weaponry, already established as the premiere experts in C3 computer integration for heavy Combine BattleMechs, positioned the Ninja-To as a fast, hard-hitting platform that could leverage shared targeting data to maximize its effectiveness within a networked lance.

The design's emphasis on speed over firepower was intentional, reflecting the Combine's doctrine that C3 network accuracy bonuses could transform a modestly armed 'Mech into a genuine threat at extended engagement ranges.
fluff.capabilities:
Weighing sixty-five tons, the Ninja-To features an extra-light Magna 390 XL engine that propels the 'Mech to a top speed of just over ninety-seven kilometers per hour, matching or exceeding many Clan medium 'Mechs of comparable mass. This remarkable speed comes at a cost, however, as the extralight engine makes the design vulnerable to destruction from side torso hits. The chassis employs Star League XT NJT Light Endo Steel construction, which lightens the frame and frees mass for weapons and armor. Twelve tons of Durallex Heavy armor with CASE protect the Ninja-To from enemy fire and internal ammunition explosions, providing reasonable survivability for a heavy 'Mech that prefers to engage at range.

The Ninja-To's armament centers on two Diverse Optics Sunbeam extended-range large lasers supplemented by two Diverse Optics ER medium lasers and a single Shigunga MRM-10 launcher. While this weapon load is modest for a sixty-five-ton design, the 'Mech's Garret T-19G communications system integrates a C3 slave unit that is the heart of the design philosophy. When linked to a C3 command network, the Ninja-To's MechWarrior can achieve accuracy at extended ranges that would otherwise be impossible, transforming limited firepower into a genuine threat. The design's twelve double-strength heat sinks are barely adequate, and heavy use of the primary weapons can quickly overtax the cooling system.
fluff.history:
The Ninja-To's genesis at Independence Weaponry traces directly to the Draconis Combine's aggressive adoption of C3 computer technology during the late 3050s. Independence Weaponry had already established itself as the leading manufacturer of C3-equipped heavy 'Mechs for the DCMS, producing designs like the Naginata, Shugenja, and Tai-sho. The Ninja-To was conceived to fill a specific gap in the Combine's C3 doctrine: a fast heavy platform that could exploit network targeting data while operating at the fringes of engagement ranges.

Production began at a modest rate in 3062, with Independence Weaponry contracted to provide the first three production runs exclusively to the DCMS. The initial shipments went to the Genyosha regiments, where both the Tai-sho and Shugenja were first assigned. Independence Weaponry executives indicated that once the supply of Ninja-Tos caught up with the existing C3 command units, the company intended to offer C3 command lance discount incentive packages combining the Shugenja, Tai-sho, Naginata, and Ninja-To as matched sets, giving customers the most of the C3 computer network advantage.

The Jihad disrupted these plans severely. Quentin fell under Word of Blake control, and the Independence Weaponry facility shifted to Blakist production priorities. During this period, the Combine turned to its mobile factory ships DCS Yamato and DCS Ryuu, jointly operated by Luthien Armor Works and Independence Weaponry, which maintained production of the NJT-3 and later developed the NJT-4 variant. These factory ships provided a vital alternative production source through the Jihad and into the early Republic era.

Following the Jihad, Quentin passed through Republic of the Sphere control before eventually returning to Combine hands, but the Independence Weaponry facility did not resume Ninja-To production. The destruction of the factory ships Yamato and Ryuu by the Ghost Bear fleet in 3099 eliminated the last remaining production line, effectively ending new manufacture of the design. Despite this, surviving Ninja-Tos remain in service across several Combine formations, their speed and C3 integration continuing to make them valued components of networked lances.
fluff.deployment: Introduced in 3075, this variant mounts a Snub-Nose PPC in each arm, replacing the original laser armament. The removal of one heat sink creates space for an advanced targeting computer that dramatically improves the accuracy of both particle projector cannons. Standard armor is replaced with Durallex Super Medium ferro-fibrous plating, providing equivalent protection at reduced weight. Produced exclusively aboard the Combine mobile factory ships during the Jihad, this variant was developed to maximize damage output at medium and close ranges where the C3 network provides the greatest accuracy advantage.
fluff.manufacturer: DCS Yamato & DCS Ryuu (LAW & Independence Weaponry)
